domain: Historical Linguistics / Language Revitalization / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Hebrew's transformation from liturgical preservation to native daily speech (late 19th-20th century), examining whether the 'Hebrew is a living language' commitment was continuously occupied across two millennia or underwent a strict-reachability break requiring reconstruction. The kernel contest centers on whether liturgical recitation constitutes occupancy of the living-language kernel or whether only native generative competence does.

key_entities: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda (revivalist architect, lexical expansion agent)
Zionist settlement institutions (kindergartens, schools enforcing Hebrew-only)
key_tensions: Liturgical preservation (symbol recitation) vs native generation (daily speech production)
Continuity claim (unbroken chain) vs reconstruction claim (strict-reachability break)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Hebrew as a living language — the claim that Hebrew occupies the status of a language with native speakers capable of generative daily use
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between rabbinic custodians (liturgical authority) and revivalist institutions (native-speaker production authority)

readings.commitment: Hebrew remains living through unbroken liturgical recitation and textual study across diaspora
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic tradition; preservation of sacred texts as sufficient occupancy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low extractiveness (symbol preservation); no victim set (voluntary participation); continuity claim valid; no strict-reachability break

readings.commitment: Hebrew becomes living only when native speakers produce daily speech generatively, not via memorized recitation
readings.authority_grounding: Revivalist institutions (Ben-Yehuda, kindergartens); linguistic nativism criterion
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness (suppression of Yiddish/Ladino); victim set includes non-Hebrew vernacular speakers; strict-reachability break acknowledged; reconstruction required

readings.commitment: Hebrew lives through Haskalah literary production — written generative competence without native daily speech
readings.expected_structural_delta: Very low extractiveness (elite literary practice); no victim set; partial continuity (written chain unbroken); ambiguous on strict-reachability

axes.structural_delta: Unbroken liturgical recitation and textual study constitute sufficient occupancy of the living-language kernel across two millennia
axes.primary_observable: Continuity of liturgical practice; rabbinic textual commentary production; absence of generational transmission break
axes.selection_reason: First reading: establishes continuity baseline against which reconstruction claim is measured

axes.structural_delta: Living-language status requires native speakers with generative daily-speech competence; liturgical recitation is insufficient; strict-reachability break occurred requiring reconstruction
axes.primary_observable: Presence of native speakers (first generation born into Hebrew-only households); lexical expansion for modern domains; suppression of competing vernaculars
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: highest centrality; introduces extractiveness and victim set; core analytical tension

axes.human_readable: Literary Revival Reading (Written Competence as Intermediate)
axes.structural_delta: Haskalah literary production demonstrates generative written competence without native daily speech; occupies intermediate position between liturgical preservation and full revival
axes.primary_observable: Volume of secular Hebrew literature (18th-19th c.); lexical innovation in written form; absence of native-speaker households
axes.selection_reason: Third reading: structural intermediate; disambiguates written vs spoken competence; completes triadic kernel decomposition

axes.human_readable: Phonological Reconstruction Gap (Lost Pronunciation as Strict Break)
axes.structural_delta: Loss of native phonological intuition (vowel points, stress patterns) constitutes irreversible strict-reachability break regardless of textual continuity
axes.primary_observable: Divergence between Ashkenazi/Sephardi/Yemenite pronunciation traditions; modern Israeli Hebrew phonology as constructed compromise
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: phonological dimension captured within native_generation_reading's reconstruction claim; independent axis would over-split

axes.human_readable: Institutional Enforcement Mechanism (Hebrew-Only Kindergartens as Coercion)

axes.primary_observable: Documented Hebrew-only policies in early Zionist schools; testimonies of Yiddish-speaking children punished for non-Hebrew speech
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: enforcement mechanism is downstream consequence of native_generation_reading commitment; captured in that reading's extractiveness analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Loss of native phonological intuition as irreversible strict-reachability break
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Phonological dimension subsumed within native_generation_reading's reconstruction analysis; independent axis would over-split the kernel

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Hebrew-only institutional policies suppressing competing vernaculars
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Enforcement mechanism is downstream implementation of native_generation_reading commitment; extractiveness captured in that reading's victim-set analysis

omegas.description: Does liturgical recitation without native generative competence constitute 'living' language status? The three readings emit incompatible answers. Liturgical reading says yes (rope, no victim set). Native reading says no (tangled_rope, Yiddish speakers as victims). Literary reading occupies intermediate position (written generation without native speech). No empirical test resolves this — it is a definitional contest over what 'living' means.

Library verdict context flags D1 strict-reachability break. Native_generation_reading accepts this verdict (reconstruction required). Liturgical_continuity_reading rejects it (unbroken chain). Literary_revival_reading is ambiguous (written chain unbroken, spoken chain broken). The verdict itself is a reading-dependent claim, not an external fact.

If native_generation_reading is correct, victim set includes Yiddish/Ladino speakers suppressed by Hebrew-only policies. If liturgical_continuity_reading is correct, no victim set exists (voluntary participation). Extractiveness measurement depends on which reading is adopted as ground truth.
omegas.source: Beneficiary scan (Dark Matter Probe 3); reading-dependent epsilon

omegas.description: Does Haskalah literary revival constitute a bridge (scaffold) between liturgical preservation and native revival, or is it a separate failed attempt at revival? Literary_revival_reading treats it as sufficient occupancy. Native_generation_reading treats it as insufficient (no native speakers produced). Structural role depends on reading.
omegas.source: Literary_revival_reading analysis; scaffold vs rope classification ambiguity

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successfully identified three structurally distinct readings with non-collapsing constraint profiles. Liturgical reading (rope, v_low ε, no victim set) vs native reading (tangled_rope, mod ε, victim set present) vs literary reading (scaffold, v_low ε, intermediate position) emit genuinely different constraints from the same kernel. User-provided strict-reachability verdict is itself reading-dependent, documented in omega_strict_reachability_verdict.
